High-confidence miRNA-mRNA interactions were obtained from miRDip, miRNA-lncRNA associations from miRNet, and TF annotations from AnimalTFDB. Functional enrichment analyses were conducted to identify overrepresented biological themes. Network topology and module structure were evaluated in Cytoscape using CytoHubba and MCODE. Integration of interaction datasets identified 179 mRNAs targeted by 93 miRNAs, of which 90 miRNAs were connected to 404 annotated lncRNAs. Twenty-five TFs were incorporated into the regulatory framework. Degree-based analysis highlighted QKI, hsa-miR-497-5p, and KCNQ1OT1 as the most connected nodes within their respective categories. Module detection revealed five densely interconnected sub-networks, indicating coordinated regulatory organization. Several prioritized elements have previously been implicated in immune or inflammatory regulation, supporting the biological relevance of the network. This integrative analysis delineates a comprehensive regulatory landscape of RA and provides a ranked set of candidate molecules for future experimental validation. Among these, CCDC6 was identified as a downregulated gene positioned within a highly connected module and linked to multiple hub miRNAs and lncRNAs, suggesting potential functional importance in RA pathobiology.

title: Hepatic Orosomucoid 2 aggravates demyelination and drives microglial DAM-like activation.
abstract: Demyelination is a central pathological feature of white matter injury (WMI). Emerging evidence suggests that hepatokines act as systemic regulators of brain pathology, raising the possibility that liver-derived signals contribute to WMI. Here, we investigated whether hepatokine Orosomucoid 2 (ORM2) aggravates demyelination through liver-brain communication by modulating disease-associated microglia (DAM)-like activation in WMI. ORM2 expression was assessed in the cuprizone (CPZ) demyelination model using RNA sequencing, quantitative PCR, western blotting, and immunofluorescence. The functional role of ORM2 in WMI was examined using ORM2 knockout mice, hepatocyte-specific ORM2 transgenic mice, and hepatocyte-targeted ORM2 knockdown strategies, combined with behavioral analyses and histological evaluation of myelin integrity. Transcriptomic profiling, lipid staining, and microglial phenotyping were performed to characterize DAM-associated responses. CPZ-induced demyelinating challenge was accompanied by robust hepatic ORM2 induction and increased cerebral ORM2 protein accumulation. Flag-tagged ORM2 tracing showed that hepatocyte-derived ORM2 could be detected in the injured brain after CPZ-induced white matter injury. ORM2 deficiency alleviated, whereas hepatocyte-specific ORM2 overexpression exacerbated, demyelination and behavioral deficits. Hepatocyte-targeted knockdown of ORM2 reduced cerebral ORM2 accumulation and mitigated white matter pathology, supporting a peripheral contribution of hepatic ORM2 to WMI. Transcriptomic and histological analyses revealed that ORM2 promoted inflammatory and DAM-like microglial programs. Mechanistically, ORM2 promoted activation of the SYK-PLCγ2 signaling axis, thereby driving DAM-like activation, lipid-associated dysregulation, and myelin loss. Our findings identify hepatic ORM2 as a pro-inflammatory hepatokine that aggravates WMI through liver-brain communication. By enhancing SYK-PLCγ2 signaling and driving DAM-like microglial activation, ORM2 links peripheral hepatic stress to central demyelination, highlighting hepatic ORM2 as a potential therapeutic target for white matter disorders.

title: EIF3B is associated with m6A-related regulation of E2F7 and promotes stemness in glioblastoma multiforme.
abstract: E2F transcription factors are key regulators of the cell cycle and play an important role in tumorigenesis. N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most prevalent internal RNA modification in eukaryotic cells, is also crucial for cancer progression. However, the interplay between E2F family members and m6A modification in glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) remains poorly understood. We applied weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify m6A-related gene modules co-expressed with E2F7, a gene that is significantly associated with adverse prognosis and tumor stemness. Through intersection analysis, eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit B (EIF3B) emerged as a hub gene, showing a strong positive correlation with E2F7 in GBM datasets. Functional validation was performed in GBM cells to assess the regulatory relationship between EIF3B and E2F7, including examination of mRNA and protein expression, mRNA stability, and m6A modification levels. GBM stemness was evaluated by tumor sphere formation assays and detection of stemness-associated markers. Functional validation revealed that EIF3B knockdown reduced E2F7 mRNA and protein expression, promoted E2F7 mRNA degradation, and decreased its m6A modification, suggesting an association between EIF3B and m6A-related regulation of E2F7 stability. Furthermore, EIF3B knockdown markedly suppressed GBM stemness, as demonstrated by impaired tumor sphere formation and downregulation of stemness-associated markers. Clinically, EIF3B expression increased with glioma grade and correlated with poor prognosis. Collectively, these findings suggest that the EIF3B-E2F7 axis is associated with m6A-related regulation in GBM and may warrant further investigation as a candidate for therapeutic targeting.

title: Circ_FAM210A regulates the malignant biological behaviour of NSCLC through the miR-670-5p/SYNE3/apoptotic pathway axis.
abstract: This study aimed to explore the effects of circ_FAM210A on the migration and invasion of NSCLC cells through the miR-670-5p/SYNE3/apoptotic pathway axis. The expressions of circ_FAM210A, miR-670-5p, and SYNE3 in NSCLC cells and tissues were analysed using RT‒qPCR. circ_FAM210A was characterized by Sanger sequencing, actinomycin D treatment, and RNA digestion assays. Nuclear‒cytoplasmic separation and FISH were performed to determine the distribution of circ_FAM210A. Cell models of NSCLC (A549 and H1299) were established. The effects of upregulation of circ_FAM210A expression and downregulation of miR-670-5p expression on the malignant progression of NSCLC were assessed via plate colony formation, cell scratch repair, chamber assays, apoptosis analysis, and protein band detection. The interactions between miR-670-5p and SYNE3 or circ_FAM210A were examined using dual-luciferase and RIP assays. Rescue experiments were conducted to analyse the regulatory effect of the circ_FAM210A/miR-670-5p/SYNE3 axis on NSCLC development. In vivo experiments were conducted to explore the effect of circ_FAM210A on tumours in mice. In NSCLC cells and tissues, the expression of circ_FAM210A and SYNE3 decreased, whereas the expression of miR-670-5p significantly increased. Circ_FAM210A is highly stable and is mostly distributed in the cytoplasm of A549 and H1299 cells. Both the downregulation of miR-670-5p expression and the overexpression of circ_FAM210A inhibited the proliferation, migration and invasion of NSCLC cells and promoted apoptosis as well as the activity of apoptotic signals. miR-670-5p directly binds to circ_FAM210A and SYNE3. The inhibition of SYNE3 reversed the cell inhibition mediated by miR-670-5p knockdown. Furthermore, overexpression of miR-670-5p or knockdown of SYNE3 abrogated the suppressive effects of circ_FAM210A on NSCLC growth and invasion. In vivo experiments demonstrated that upregulation of circ_FAM210A expression reduced both the size and weight of tumours in mice. Upregulation of circ_FAM210A expression can inhibit the malignant progression of NSCLC, partly through the miR-670-5p/SYNE3/apoptotic pathway axis.

title: ExoU-Mediated Host-Cell Cytotoxicity is Associated with Phosphorylation-Dependent Regulation of DDX3Y during Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection.
abstract: The Pseudomonas aeruginosa type III secretion system effector ExoU is a potent phospholipase A2 that causes rapid host-cell injury, but how it engages intracellular host networks during infection remains incompletely understood. Here, using an endogenously Flag-tagged infection model in male-derived A549 cells, we identified MYH6 and DDX3Y as ExoU-associated host factors. Knockdown of either protein reduced PA14-induced cytotoxicity, indicating that both contribute to the cellular response to ExoU-positive P. aeruginosa. An in vitro pull-down assay using purified proteins further supported a direct but relatively weak association between ExoU-S142A and DDX3Y. Quantitative phosphoproteomic analysis revealed extensive host phosphorylation changes associated with ExoU catalytic activity and identified multiple phosphorylation sites on DDX3Y. Phosphorylation at S506 was detected following PA14 infection but not following exoU-S142A infection. Phospho-deficient DDX3Y mutants at S101, S141, and S506 showed increased association with ExoU, whereas the combined S101A/S141A/S506A mutant further enhanced this association and reduced infection-induced cytotoxicity. Conversely, the phosphomimetic S506E mutant showed reduced association with ExoU and restored cytotoxicity relative to S506A. RNA sequencing and DDX3Y RIP analyses further showed that ExoU catalytic activity was associated with a broader inflammatory transcriptional response and with changes in the DDX3Y-bound transcriptome, including altered association with IL6ST and NFKBIZ transcripts. Together, these findings identify MYH6 and DDX3Y as distinct ExoU-associated host factors and support a model in which ExoU catalytic activity is linked to multisite regulation of DDX3Y, altered ExoU-DDX3Y association, and changes in DDX3Y-associated RNAs. These results extend the current understanding of ExoU-mediated cytotoxicity beyond direct membrane damage.

title: Spin-State Engineering of Asymmetric Fe-PN3 Single-Atom Nanozyme Enables Redox Microenvironment Reprogramming in Osteonecrosis.
abstract: Nanozymes, which mimic the catalytic activities of natural enzymes, have been investigated as therapeutic agents for treating reactive oxygen species (ROS)-related diseases. Despite progress having been made in nanozyme engineering, their diverse nanostructures and poor atom utilization efficiency severely limit further applications. Symmetric Fe-N4 coordination in iron-based single-atom nanozymes (SANs) confers intrinsic ROS scavenging activity; however, excessive adsorption of oxygen intermediates restricts catalytic turnover. Here, we describe a spin-state engineering strategy to address this limitation through asymmetric coordination design. Phosphorus incorporation transforms the symmetric Fe-N4 motif into an Fe-PN3 configuration, inducing a transition of Fe 3d orbitals from a low-spin to a high-spin state. Density functional theory calculations indicate that this spin modulation raises the count of unpaired electrons and moves the d-band center nearer the Fermi level, which in turn tunes the binding energies of oxygen intermediates and speeds up the catalytic cycle. Consequently, the Fe-PN3 nanozyme exhibits substantially enhanced ROS detoxification efficiency compared with its Fe-N4 counterpart. In a glucocorticoid-induced osteonecrosis model, the spin-engineered nanozyme modulates the pathological redox microenvironment, restores impaired autophagic flux, and preserves tissue integrity. Single-cell RNA sequencing further indicates coordinated modulation of oxidative stress-responsive and autophagy-related pathways. Collectively, this work supports asymmetric coordination-induced spin-state regulation as a strategy for designing high-performance iron-based single-atom nanozymes with translational potential in ROS-driven degenerative diseases.

title: Antiviral activity of tannic acid against porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus and transcriptomic identification of TNFAIP3 as a candidate proviral host factor.
abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) causes enormous economic losses to the global swine industry. Given the extensive viral diversity and the limited heterologous cross-protection of current vaccines, antiviral strategies with broad activity against diverse PRRSV strains are urgently needed. This study investigated the anti-PRRSV activity of tannic acid (TA), a plant-derived polyphenol. TA potently inhibited PRRSV replication in both MARC-145 cells (half-maximal inhibitory concentration [IC50] = 5.34 μM; selectivity index [SI] = 12.59) and primary porcine alveolar macrophages (IC50 = 4.22 μM; SI = 42.65) and exhibited broad activity against multiple lineages of PRRSV-2. Mode-of-action assays revealed that TA primarily exerts virucidal and post-entry inhibitory effects. RNA sequencing-based transcriptomic analysis of TA-treated, PRRSV-infected cells identified differentially expressed genes significantly enriched in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), tumor necrosis factor (TNF), and interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling pathways. Among five candidate genes selected for small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated functional validation, knockdown of TNF alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3, also known as A20) most significantly suppressed PRRSV replication. PRRSV infection markedly upregulated TNFAIP3 expression, and TA reversed this upregulation in a dose-dependent manner. TNFAIP3 silencing reduced viral RNA levels, nucleocapsid (N) protein expression, and infectious titers, with the most pronounced effect during early infection. Collectively, the findings identify TA as a potent anti-PRRSV polyphenol and reveal TNFAIP3 as a candidate proviral host factor that is upregulated during PRRSV infection, providing insights into virus-host interactions and potential targets for host-directed antiviral strategies.

title: Rethinking nonsense suppression therapies in inherited retinal diseases.
abstract: Nonsense mutations account for approximately 20% of pathogenic variants in inherited retinal diseases (IRDs). With advances in gene therapy, nucleic acid-based nonsense suppression strategies, including suppressor tRNAs, RNA pseudouridylation, and adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, have demonstrated therapeutic potential in preclinical studies. These next-generation approaches offer substantial opportunities for engineering and optimization, with the potential to enable precise and efficient restoration of full-length functional proteins. In this review, we propose that IRDs represent an attractive group of diseases for the clinical translation of these next-generation therapies owing to their high burden of nonsense mutations and the unique advantages of ocular gene therapy. We further outline key strategies to accelerate clinical translation, spanning therapeutic engineering, preclinical validation, and mutation-guided clinical trial design.

title: Single-Cell Resolution Mapping Reveals Cell Death-Associated Stress Programs and Osteogenic-Chondrogenic Differentiation Imbalance in Subchondral Bone Mesenchymal Stem Cells of Knee Osteoarthritis.
abstract: KOA is a degenerative joint disorder characterized by progressive cartilage degradation and subchondral bone remodeling. Subchondral bone MSCs orchestrate tissue homeostasis through osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiation, yet the mechanisms underlying their lineage imbalance in OA pathogenesis remain poorly understood. We reanalyzed publicly available human tibial-plateau subchondral-bone single-cell RNA-sequencing and bulk-expression datasets using library-aware integration, donor-paired regional pseudobulk summaries, diffusion pseudotime, candidate cell-cell interaction analysis, and weighted gene co-expression analysis. Quantitative RT-PCR in four ATCC cell lines (NHAC, SW1353, MG-63, and U2OS) assessed ferroptosis-related gene expression (GPX4, SLC7A11, ACSL4, and TFRC). Immunofluorescence with COL2A1 co-staining and Western blotting assessed protein-level changes across four experimental groups (Control, OA, OA + OE-GPX4, and OA + si-GPX4). After quality control, 25,885 of 31,090 cells were retained and assigned to 12 marker-supported display labels. The single-cell analysis defined eight molecular program modules, whereas the bulk analysis identified six data-derived coexpression blocks. Donor-paired regional analyses characterized observed composition and expression differences, and diffusion pseudotime organized 749 mesenchymal/perivascular stromal cells without establishing lineage conversion. Bulk OA-versus-Normal analysis identified 1,805 differentially expressed genes, and the exploratory cross-platform comparison showed no global monotonic correspondence (Spearman rho = 0.009, p = 0.282). Quantitative RT-PCR showed lower GPX4 and SLC7A11 and higher ACSL4 and TFRC in OA-like chondrocytes, whereas osteosarcoma lines showed higher GPX4, SLC7A11, and TFRC. Immunofluorescence and Western blotting showed corresponding GPX4, SLC7A11, and ACSL4 changes across the four experimental groups, with COL2A1 co-staining providing a matrix-associated readout. Integrated single-cell and bulk analyses identified regional transcriptional patterns, stromal-state ordering, and stress-associated programs in subchondral bone. In vitro assays supported ferroptosis-related protein changes in OA-like chondrocytes. These findings provide candidate mechanisms for further functional testing but do not establish lineage conversion or causal relationships.

title: TRIP13 Promotes Aflatoxin B1-Induced Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Inhibiting Ferroptosis.
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a potent foodborne hepatocarcinogen that contributes substantially to the global burden of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the molecular mechanisms underlying AFB1-driven HCC progression remain incompletely understood. In this study, we identified thyroid hormone receptor-interacting protein 13 (TRIP13) as an important contributor to AFB1-related HCC progression and investigated its involvement in ferroptosis regulation. TCGA-LIHC, GSE25844, and single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE166635) revealed that TRIP13 was significantly upregulated in AFB1-related HCC, enriched in malignant cell populations, and associated with poor clinical outcomes. In Huh7 cells, AFB1 treatment markedly increased TRIP13 expression, while TRIP13 knockdown significantly suppressed AFB1-induced cell proliferation, colony formation, migration, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Bulk RNA sequencing and pathway enrichment analyses indicated that TRIP13 overexpression was strongly associated with ferroptosis-related signaling. Mechanistically, TRIP13 was associated with ferroptosis resistance through modulation of the KEAP1/NRF2/xCT/GPX4 pathway, thereby contributing to redox homeostasis during AFB1 exposure. Consistently, TRIP13 knockdown restored ferroptotic sensitivity, as evidenced by increased Fe2+ and malondialdehyde levels and altered glutathione metabolism. Importantly, ferroptosis induction with RSL3 effectively reversed the pro-tumor effects of TRIP13 overexpression both in vitro and in vivo, including enhanced proliferation, EMT, migration, and xenograft tumor growth. Collectively, these findings suggest that TRIP13 contributes to AFB1-associated HCC progression through ferroptosis-related regulation and highlight the AFB1/TRIP13/ferroptosis axis as a potential molecular mechanism and candidate target for further investigation in AFB1-related HCC.

title: DNA Tetrahedral Nanoprobes-Based Logic-Gated FRET Sensor for in Situ Analysis of Dual MicroRNAs in Extracellular Vesicles.
abstract: Conventional analysis of extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived microRNAs relies on vesicle lysis and RNA extraction, which disrupt native vesicular structure and eliminate intravesicular molecular cargoes. Here, we report a rigid DNA tetrahedral nanoprobes-based logic-gated Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) platform for in situ, amplification-free detection of dual miRNAs directly within intact EVs. Tetrahedral DNA nanostructures (TDNs) targeting miR-21 and miR-141 were engineered with concealed sticky ends that become exposed upon target binding, triggering conditional interparticle assembly and FRET activation exclusively under dual-input conditions. This design physically implements an AND logic operation, converting miRNA coexpression into unified ratiometric output. The rigid tetrahedral scaffold constrains fluorophore spacing and reduces conformational entropy, enabling precise distance-modulated signal transduction with a detection limit of 12.86 pM for dual miRNAs without enzymatic amplification. In clinical plasma samples from 20 prostate cancer (PCa) patients and 20 healthy controls, the ratiometric FRET signal achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.903 and 85.0% diagnostic accuracy, outperforming single-channel measurements. By integrating structural programmability with molecular logic sensor, this strategy transforms EV biomarker analysis from independent signal acquisition into intrinsic nanoscale information processing, establishing a robust platform for noninvasive liquid biopsy.

title: Molecular epidemiological characteristics and pathogenicity of Chinese PRRSV-2 L1B sublineage strains in piglets.
abstract: PRRSV evolves through mutation and recombination during circulation, contributing to the emergence and spread of genetically diverse lineages. Among these, the PRRSV-2 L1B sublineage has been detected in multiple countries, but its molecular epidemiology and pathogenicity remain poorly characterized. We investigated the molecular epidemiology of L1B PRRSV in China and assessed its pathogenicity in piglets. L1B strains were detected in multiple Chinese provinces. Phylogenetic analysis based on the ORF5 sequences revealed that all Chinese L1B PRRSV strains cluster within the L1B sublineage of PRRSV-2. These strains harbor a 131-amino-acid discontinuous deletion (111+1+19) in the Nsp2 protein and carry cluster-associated amino acid substitutions at positions 137 and 178 of the GP5 protein. Whole-genome analysis revealed that Chinese L1B strains possess complex genetic backgrounds, likely arising from recombination between indigenous circulating strains (NADC30-like and HP-PRRSV) and the introduced L1B strains. Animal challenge experiments demonstrated that inoculation with the representative isolate TZJ2547 induced clinical symptoms including fever, coughing, and decreased feed intake, accompanied by persistent viremia, high viral RNA loads in multiple tissues, and pathological lesions in the lungs and lymphoid tissues. These findings indicate that TZJ2547 exhibits moderate pathogenicity in the challenged piglets. This study characterizes the epidemiological distribution, genomic characteristics, and recombination profile of L1B PRRSV in China. To the best of our knowledge, this study reports the first systematic pathogenicity evaluation of a Chinese L1B PRRSV isolate in piglets. Collectively, these findings provide fundamental data to inform the surveillance and control of this viral sublineage.

title: 3D tissue model to patient atlas: dynamic network topology reveals PDAC chemoresistance bottlenecks.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) develops chemoresistance through dynamic cell-state transitions, yet the regulatory network architecture governing drug-tolerant states remains poorly characterised, because static expression snapshots cannot capture how interaction topology evolves along treatment-induced trajectories. We established a 3D PANC-1 tissue model on decellularised porcine intestinal matrix, which reaches patient-like proliferation indices and tissue-niche-specific drug responses, and performed single-cell RNA sequencing across four conditions: control, gemcitabine (GEM), TGF-β1, and their combination. Coupling pseudotime trajectory inference to dynamic protein-protein interaction network analysis, we tracked betweenness centrality continuously across cell-state transitions rather than comparing discrete states. GEM survivors engaged a proliferative programme (E2F1, CDK1, AURKA, TPX2, TOP2A, BIRC5), whereas TGF-β1 induced an independent EMT attractor (SPOCK1, MBOAT2, COL5A1, THBS1, FN1). Where the two converged, an emergent bottleneck appeared: CDK1 betweenness centrality spiked selectively, restrained by CDKN1A (p21) and WEE1, defining an S-phase-persistence state enriched for GEM survivors. Cross-examination in a PDAC atlas of 726,107 cells from 231 patients showed 8.7-fold metastatic enrichment of triple-positive cells. This framework, linking controlled 3D tissue experimentation, single-cell systems analysis and clinical-scale patient data, is applicable to drug resistance across cancer types.

title: Polystyrene Nanoplastics Disrupt Lateral Line Neuromasts and Impair Flow-Guided Behaviors in Zebrafish.
abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) are pervasive aquatic pollutants; however, their effects on fish mechanosensory function remain poorly understood. This study investigated the impacts of polystyrene NPs (PS-NPs) on the lateral line system of zebrafish (Danio rerio) across life stages by integrating hydrodynamic behavioral assays with cellular, ultrastructural, transcriptomic, and protein-level analyses. Our results showed that PS-NP exposure significantly impaired flow-guided behaviors and hydrodynamic sensing in both life stages. Adult zebrafish exhibited reduced trajectory linearity and directional precision during rheotaxis, while larvae showed compromised spatial stability and elevated angular motion under vortex-flow conditions. These functional alterations were accompanied by reduced DASPEI-positive hair-cell counts, increased apoptosis, shortened kinocilia, and disorganization and partial loss of apical hair bundles. Integrated bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing revealed consistent perturbations in pathways related to mitochondrial bioenergetics, glutathione metabolism, AMPK/mTOR-associated signaling, cytoskeletal organization, and vesicle trafficking. Whole-larva protein analysis further showed increased LC3B and ACSL4 abundance and decreased GPX4 abundance, consistent with autophagy- and ferroptosis-associated molecular alterations. In conclusion, these results identify the lateral line as a sensitive target of NP exposure and suggest that PS-NPs may impair hydrodynamic sensing through neuromast structural damage and metabolic-redox dysregulation.

title: SPP1⁺ macrophage-derived WNT5A contributes to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the stromal-immune circuits that coordinate matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the stromal-immune interactions associated with LUAD progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade. Bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic data were integrated with clinical immunotherapy cohorts. Weighted gene co‑expression network analysis, survival meta‑analysis, and tissue enrichment scoring identified high‑risk cell subpopulations. Cell‑cell communication, virtual gene knockout, and spatial deconvolution were used to predict ligand‑receptor interactions and colocalization. Multiplex immunohistochemistry of clinical specimens validated spatial relationships. In vitro, MMP11-overexpressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and SPP1-overexpressing macrophages (Macs) were generated, and a macrophage-CAF co‑culture system was constructed. Migration, contractility, extracellular matrix deposition, and YAP/INHBA pathway activation was measured. In vivo, a murine tumor model was established and evaluated using in vivo imaging, flow cytometry, atomic force microscopy assay, HE, masson staining, and multiplexed IHC staining. MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic CAF (MMP11⁺ myCAF) was identified as a high-risk CAF subset enriched in primary tumor and metastatic lesions, characterized by elevated expression of matrix-remodeling and contractile genes, including MMP11, ACTA2, and TAGLN. Increased abundance of MMP11⁺ myCAF was associated with advanced tumor stage, metastasis, poor overall survival, and reduced benefit from immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Spatial transcriptomic deconvolution and multiplex immunohistochemistry revealed that MMP11⁺ myCAFs spatially co-localized with SPP1⁺ Mac, a pro-tumor myeloid population enriched in malignant and metastatic LUAD tissues. Ligand-receptor and downstream target analyses identified WNT5A as a key macrophage-derived mediator linking SPP1⁺ Mac to MMP11⁺ myCAF activation. Mechanistically, SPP1⁺ Mac exhibited activation of NFKB2/RELB-associated transcriptional programs, and SPP1 overexpression increased Nfkb2, Relb, and WNT5A protein levels in macrophages. WNT5A stimulation promoted YAP/INHBA-associated signaling in CAFs, enhancing CAF migration, contractility and extracellular matrix deposition. In animal models, activation of WNT5A signaling impaired the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1 blockade, reduced intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and increased MMP11⁺ CAF-associated collagen deposition and tissue stiffness. SPP1⁺ Mac-derived WNT5A may contribute to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy to overcome ICB resistance.

title: Defining early human developmental identity: A curated, cross-platform marker framework.
abstract: Early human development involves dynamic cell-state transitions, complicating distinction between transient transcriptional changes and stable lineage commitment in human pluripotent stem cell models. To address this challenge, we establish a curated, cross-platform marker framework for pluripotency and early germ-layer identity. Starting from an unbiased RNA-seq discovery set, we validated candidates by qPCR and evaluated the panel across independent bulk RNA-seq and embryonic single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets. This yielded 67 validated markers, of which 66 were retained for downstream transcriptomic analyses. Our framework identified early developmental states across heterogeneous datasets and showed lineage-associated enrichment in human and macaque embryonic references despite substantial transcriptional variability. Protein-level concordance was observed for detectable targets in KOLF2.1J proteomic data. To enable broad application, we introduce DeepDiff, a web-based resource integrating the marker framework and enabling automated fate classification. Together, this work provides a transferable framework for assessing early developmental identity across experimental contexts.

title: Fhl2 promotes chondrocyte ferroptosis in osteoarthritis by impairing mitophagic flux through microtubule disorganization.
abstract: Ferroptosis contributes to osteoarthritis (OA), but the upstream mechanisms connecting cytoskeletal stress, mitochondrial quality control, and antioxidant defense remain unclear. We investigated whether four-and-a-half LIM domain protein 2 (Fhl2) couples microtubule remodeling to chondrocyte ferroptosis. Public bulk and single-cell transcriptomes were integrated with RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) from RSL3-treated chondrocytes to nominate ferroptosis regulators in OA. Fhl2 was validated in human cartilage, destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) mouse cartilage, and interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β)- or RSL3-treated primary murine chondrocytes. Lentiviral Fhl2 knockdown, microtubule imaging, mitochondria-lysosome co-localization, mitophagy marker analysis, paclitaxel/nocodazole perturbation, intra-articular sh-Fhl2 delivery, and cartilage-specific nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) conditional knockout were used to define mechanism and in vivo relevance. Fhl2 emerged as a shared hub across OA bulk signatures, chondrocyte states prone to ferroptosis, and the RSL3-induced ferroptosis program, and was elevated in human OA cartilage, DMM cartilage, and stressed chondrocytes. Fhl2 upregulation accompanied microtubule disorganization, impaired mitophagic flux, translocase of outer mitochondrial membrane 20 (TOMM20)/p62/microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B) accumulation, mitochondrial retention, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and lipid peroxidation. Fhl2 knockdown preserved microtubules, improved mitochondria-lysosome coupling, reduced ferroptotic injury, attenuated cartilage degeneration after DMM, improved gait parameters, and restored Nrf2/glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) signaling. Nrf2 deficiency was associated with matrix catabolism and a ferroptosis-prone cartilage phenotype after DMM. Fhl2 promotes chondrocyte ferroptosis in OA by linking impaired microtubule-dependent mitophagic flux to mitochondrial retention and antioxidant failure. Targeting the link between Fhl2, cytoskeletal integrity, and mitochondrial quality control may help limit cartilage degeneration driven by ferroptosis.

title: LncRNA MIR4435-2HG confers radioresistance in NSCLC by sponging miR-1-3p to upregulate DNA-PKcs and selectively promote NHEJ repair.
abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are critical regulators of tumor radiosensitivity and hold promise as novel targets for radiosensitization. However, the underlying mechanisms by which most lncRNAs modulate radiosensitivity remain elusive. This study aimed to elucidate the functional significance and mechanistic basis of lncRNA MIR4435-2HG in regulating non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) radiosensitivity. Our findings demonstrated that ionizing radiation induced upregulation of lncRNA MIR4435-2HG. High expression of MIR4435-2HG was significantly associated with poor prognosis in patients with lung adenocarcinoma. Inhibition of MIR4435-2HG increased the radiosensitivity of NSCLC cells. Mechanistically, MIR4435-2HG acted as a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) to sponge miR-1-3p, thereby derepressing DNA-PKcs at both mRNA and protein levels. Knockdown of MIR4435-2HG impaired non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) repair, as evidenced by increased 53BP1 and γH2AX foci, reduced interaction of DNA-PKcs with Ku70 and XRCC4, and decreased NHEJ repair efficiency. Conversely, overexpression of MIR4435-2HG induced a radioresistant phenotype. Dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed the interaction between miR-1-3p and both MIR4435-2HG and DNA-PKcs. Rescue experiments confirmed that miR-1-3p overexpression reversed MIR4435-2HG-mediated DNA-PKcs upregulation, proliferation enhancement, and radioresistance. Notably, MIR4435-2HG selectively promoted error-prone NHEJ without affecting homologous recombination. In summary, our study delineates a novel and functionally specific ceRNA axis wherein MIR4435-2HG sequesters miR-1-3p to upregulate DNA-PKcs and selectively activate NHEJ-mediated DSB repair. These findings not only introduce a critical regulatory node into the DNA repair network but also position the MIR4435-2HG/miR-1-3p/DNA-PKcs axis as a promising predictive biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming radioresistance in NSCLC.

title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals Candidate Serum Biomarkers Linked to Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Mediated Extracellular Matrix Remodeling in Metastatic Gastric Cancer.
abstract: Metastatic gastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, while currently available serum biomarkers have limited performance for metastatic risk assessment. This study aimed to identify candidate serum biomarkers associated with gastric cancer progression through quantitative proteomics and integrated multi-omics analysis. Serum data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics was performed in patients with metastatic gastric cancer and healthy controls, followed by integration with TCGA-STAD survival analysis and multi-algorithm machine-learning modelling to identify clinically relevant candidates. Single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and cell-cell communication analyses were further applied to characterize the tumor microenvironmental context of candidate genes. Serum ITIH3 levels were validated by ELISA in healthy controls, non-metastatic gastric cancer, lymph-node-only metastatic gastric cancer, and distant metastatic gastric cancer groups. Proteomic analysis identified 45 differentially expressed proteins, and ITIH3, VWF, SH3BGRL3, and PKLR were prioritized through integrated analyses. Single-cell analyses indicated that ITIH3 expression was mainly associated with cancer-associated fibroblast-related extracellular matrix remodeling signatures. ELISA validation demonstrated progressively increased serum ITIH3 levels during gastric cancer progression, with favorable discrimination among selected disease groups. These findings suggest that serum ITIH3 is a candidate biomarker associated with gastric cancer progression and tumor microenvironmental alterations, warranting further clinical validation.

title: Nonhistone Protein Acetylation Reprograms the ECM-Receptor Interaction Pathway: Multiomics Profiling of Cartilage Degeneration in Rat Models of Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Nonhistone acetylation is a key epigenetic mechanism in osteoarthritis (OA), but its specific role in cartilage degeneration remains unclear. Here, we integrated transcriptomics, proteomics, and acetyl-proteomics to systematically analyze molecular changes in rat OA cartilage. Multiomics coenrichment identified the ECM-receptor interaction pathway as the core target, reprogrammed by increased acetylation of Fn1, Tnc, and Itgb1. Using 113 machine-learning strategies, we identified 11 core diagnostic genes, with Wisp3 showing the highest efficacy validated in independent data sets. In vitro experiments and single-cell RNA-seq confirmed that Wisp3 downregulation disrupts ECM homeostasis. This study reveals that nonhistone acetylation drives OA by reprogramming the ECM-receptor interaction pathway and provides novel early diagnostic biomarkers.

title: Identification of key cell subpopulations and associated biomarkers for mouse dry eye disease based on the Scissor-CIBERSORTx algorithm integration strategy.
abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is characterized by tear film instability and chronic inflammation, with the cornea serving as a key target site vulnerable to inflammatory damage. This study integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomics combined with Scissor and CIBERSORTx algorithms to screen corneal key cell populations and biomarkers in murine DED. Corneal wing cells were identified as core disease-associated cells, among which interferon-response wing cells (IFN-response-wing) were the pivotal pathogenic subtype. Three IFN-response-wing signature biomarkers Upk3b, Dusp1 and Ly6e were screened, enriched in immune pathways including antigen processing and presentation, primary immunodeficiency, and cytokine receptor interaction. We constructed a chemical-induced DED mouse model for multi-layered validation via immunofluorescence, Real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and Western blot. Immunofluorescence revealed tissue-specific protein patterns: DED corneal epithelium exhibited elevated IRF1, Dusp1 and Ly6e protein yet reduced Upk3b, with Ly6e co-localized with IRF1-positive cells. However, RT-qPCR and Western blot of whole corneal tissue demonstrated significant upregulation of Upk3b, Dusp1 and Ly6e at both mRNA and total protein levels. Collectively, IFN-response-wing drives DED pathogenesis, and Upk3b, Dusp1, Ly6e act as tissue-specific DED biomarkers with inconsistent trends between epithelial localized protein and global corneal molecular abundance, providing novel mechanistic clues for DED diagnosis and targeted therapy.

title: Endothelial cell-specific TGM2 deficiency promotes progression of temporal lobe epilepsy by disrupting S1P metabolism and intercellular communication.
abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a common and medically refractory neurological disorder with a complex pathogenesis. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction is a key pathogenic factor. As a multifunctional protein, TGM2 has been shown to participate in vascular homeostasis, metabolic pathway regulation, and immune-inflammatory responses. This study aimed to systematically investigate the expression pattern, core functions, and molecular regulatory mechanisms of TGM2 in TLE, and to clarify its clinical value. Temporal cortex tissue and plasma samples from drug-resistant TLE patients and control subjects were collected, alongside kainic acid (KA)-induced epileptic mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing was adopted to identify TGM2's cell-specific expression pattern, and qPCR, Western blot and ELISA validated its expression levels. With endothelial cell-specific TGM2 conditional knockout mice, in vivo experiments assessed seizure severity and BBB permeability through behavioral observation, intracranial local field potential (LFP) recording and Evans blue (EB) assay. In vitro siRNA-mediated TGM2 knockdown in brain microvascular endothelial cells verified endothelial functional changes. Metabolomics, RNA-seq, nucleocytoplasmic separation, immunofluorescence and molecular docking were used to clarify regulatory mechanisms, and intercellular communication networks were constructed to analyze ligand-receptor interactions. Results indicated that endothelial TGM2 was significantly downregulated in TLE patients and epileptic mice. Endothelial TGM2 deficiency aggravated recurrent seizures, increased BBB permeability, impaired endothelial function, and reduced the expression of tight junction protein CLDN5. Mechanistically, TGM2 positively regulated sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) synthesis. Reduced S1P production abolished the inhibition of RelA nuclear translocation, thereby activating downstream inflammatory genes and triggering endothelial inflammation. Molecular docking confirmed the direct binding between S1P and RelA. Furthermore, TGM2 deficiency remodels endothelial-neuron-microglia communication and disrupts neural circuit homeostasis. This study establishes a link between TGM2 and BBB function, metabolic pathways, and intercellular communication in TLE, providing an experimental basis for developing TLE therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway.

title: Stromal B7-H3 Expression Characterizes an Immune-Hot Microenvironment and Predicts Response to PD-1 Blockade in Gastric Cancer.
abstract: We evaluated whether B7-H3, particularly stromal B7-H3, is associated with clinical benefit from programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade in gastric cancer (GC) and characterized the immune context underlying this association. B7-H3 expression was evaluated by conventional and multiplex immunohistochemistry (m-IHC) in a discovery cohort of 124 patients with GC receiving PD-1 inhibitor-based therapy and in an independent single-center validation cohort of 40 patients. Associations with treatment response and progression-free survival (PFS) were assessed using categorical tests, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and Cox regression. An exploratory cohort of 40 patients who had not received PD-1 blockade was analyzed to assess the general prognostic association of B7-H3. Host B7-H3 was further examined in a subcutaneous mouse forestomach carcinoma (MFC) tumor model using Cd276-deficient mice, with immune profiling and RNA sequencing after PD-1 blockade. In the discovery cohort, B7-H3 expression was significantly higher in responders (P < 0.0001), and high B7-H3 expression was associated with longer PFS (P = 0.0030). In the validation cohort, the objective response rate was 64.0% in the B7-H3-high group versus 26.7% in the B7-H3-low group (P = 0.0484), and B7-H3-high patients had longer PFS (P = 0.0315). Cell-type-specific m-IHC showed stronger associations for B7-H3+/α-SMA+, B7-H3+/CD31+, and B7-H3+/CD68+ stromal compartments than for B7-H3+/PanCK+ tumor cells. B7-H3 also correlated positively with PD-L1 and triplet cell cluster (TCC) infiltration. In the exploratory non-PD-1 cohort, high B7-H3 expression showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher mortality (HR = 1.548, 95% CI 0.932-2.571, P = 0.091). Following PD-1 blockade, wild-type tumors showed greater tumor control and higher CD8+, CD4+, and natural killer (NK)-cell infiltration than Cd276-deficient tumors. Stromal B7-H3 is a candidate biomarker associated with favorable outcomes after PD-1 blockade and may mark an immune-engaged microenvironment with pre-existing immune-cell infiltration. These findings support prospective, multicenter evaluation of B7-H3 for patient stratification rather than establishing it as a clinically validated companion diagnostic.

title: Histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomic analysis identifies an ECM-associated stromal pattern in lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma with complementary proteomic and functional analyses.
abstract: Lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) is a rare but locally aggressive malignancy characterized by perineural invasion, recurrence, and limited systemic treatment options. Although extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of tumor progression, its spatial organization and functional relevance in LGACC remain incompletely understood. A publicly available LGACC spatial transcriptomic tissue section was reanalyzed using histopathology-guided annotation to define a highly cellular Tumor Core and an adjacent stromal region, termed the Stroma Boundary. Regional differential expression and functional enrichment analyses were performed, together with module scoring, a sensitivity analysis within a shared transcriptomic cluster spanning both histopathologically defined regions, and CellChat-based ligand-receptor inference. The spatial findings were further contextualized using a public bulk RNA-sequencing cohort and an in-house quantitative proteomic cohort comparing conventional LGACC with LGACC showing high-grade transformation (LGACC-HGT). The effects of type I collagen were evaluated in SACC-LM cells using morphological assessment, CCK-8, wound-healing, Transwell migration, and Western blotting assays. Within the analyzed spatial section, Stroma Boundary spots showed higher expression of ECM-related genes, including COL1A1, COL1A2, SPARC, and DCN, together with enrichment of collagen fibril organization and extracellular matrix organization. A secondary analysis restricted to a shared transcriptomic cluster spanning both histopathologically defined regions showed that ECM-associated differences remained detectable within a more similar transcriptomic background. CellChat analysis nominated collagen-associated interactions involving CD44 as candidate components of region-to-region communication. Bulk RNA-sequencing provided contextual support for the tumor-associated transcriptional program but incompletely captured the localized stromal pattern. Proteomic profiling demonstrated increased abundance of multiple collagen- and matrix-associated proteins in LGACC-HGT, accompanied by enrichment of ECM-receptor interaction and focal adhesion-related pathways. In vitro, type I collagen induced a more dispersed and spread cellular morphology and enhanced wound closure and Transwell migration without significantly altering short-term cell viability. Collagen exposure was also associated with increased CD44 protein expression. CD44 knockdown attenuated the COL1-induced increase in wound closure, suggesting a functional contribution of CD44 to this response. Histopathology-guided spatial analysis identified an ECM-enriched regional transcriptional pattern in the stromal compartment of the analyzed LGACC section. Complementary proteomic and functional findings suggest that collagen-associated remodeling may contribute to the migratory phenotype of ACC cells. CD44 represents a biologically plausible candidate associated with the collagen response, although its mechanistic role requires further validation.

title: Characterization of the crotonylation landscape in gastric cancer: a machine learning-derived prognostic signature and the oncogenic role of TIMP1.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a lethal malignancy with high heterogeneity and poor prognosis. Crotonylation, a key post-translational modification, contributes significantly to oncogenic processes and immune system interactions; however, its prognostic significance in gastric cancer is not fully understood. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk transcriptomics to evaluate cell-specific crotonylation activity and utilized WGCNA to identify core crotonylation-related gene modules. A machine learning-derived crotonylation-related prognostic signature (CRGS) was established and validated across independent cohorts. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and immunotherapy response analyses were conducted. Furthermore, the expression and oncogenic roles of a key risk gene, TIMP1, were experimentally validated using qRT-PCR, colony formation, and Transwell migration/invasion assays. Single-cell analysis revealed significantly elevated crotonylation activity in epithelial cells. The machine learning-derived CRGS successfully stratified patients into distinct risk groups, with high-risk patients showing a severe survival disadvantage. The nomogram integrating the CRGS and clinical factors demonstrated robust prognostic accuracy. Functional analysis indicated that high-risk patients were enriched in tumor-promoting pathways, while low-risk patients exhibited enhanced immune infiltration and metabolic homeostasis. The low-risk group also exhibited elevated tumor mutational burden, stronger cancer-immunity cycle activity, and better predicted response to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Experimental validation confirmed that TIMP1 was heavily upregulated in GC cell lines. Silencing TIMP1 significantly suppressed GC cell proliferation, colony formation, migration, and invasion. Our study establishes a reliable, clinically translatable CRGS for risk stratification and immunotherapy prediction, while identifying TIMP1 as a potential therapeutic target and a key oncogenic factor in vitro in GC.
